newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy Ross leaves Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross leaves Israel.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross departed Israel on Friday night for Washington, failing to break a deadlock in Israel-Palestinian peace talks.
"He's now returning to the United States," said Richard Scorza of the spokesman for the American Embassy in Tel Aviv.
Ross held separate meetings on Friday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat before heading home.
"I think what is important is as I leave the region is that there is a very clear desire to find a way out...to finda a way to promote moving towards peace," Ross said shortly before his departure.
He said he would report to President Bill Clinton and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright upon his return to discuss how to push forward the talks, stalled for two-months.
